situation:
You are the finance lead at THISTLEDOWN FITNESS, a two-year-old operator of six franchised gyms. The chief executive (judge), who founded the company and is preparing to go back to its investors for a second round of funding, has asked you to recommend what the company does about the member billing system whose installation has run over its budget.

THISTLEDOWN FITNESS has spent most of its first round of funding. The new billing system is half installed: three gyms run on it and three are still on spreadsheets, and the two sets of numbers disagree about how many members each gym has to sign to cover its monthly costs. Finishing the installation costs more than the project has left in its budget.

One course is to finish the rollout by moving money out of the equipment replacement reserve. Moving money out of the equipment replacement reserve keeps the billing system live and every member billed correctly this quarter, and it leaves nothing set aside for the treadmills and rowers that come off the depreciation schedule early next year, when the six gyms will need them replaced.

The other course is to pause the half-installed rollout and write off what has been spent on it. Writing off what has been spent protects the equipment replacement reserve and the cash the company has left, and the write-off lands on the quarter the chief executive will show the investors when the company asks for its second round of funding.

The chief executive (judge) wants your analysis of what each course does to the number of members each gym has to sign to cover its costs, a view on what each one does to the depreciation schedule and to the numbers the company can report at all, and a recommendation. The chief executive (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the chief executive (judge) of THISTLEDOWN FITNESS. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You want the participant to analyze what finishing the rollout and what pausing it each do to the number of members each gym has to sign to cover its costs and to the depreciation schedule, and to recommend which course the company takes before it goes back to its investors.
